protections: URL adjudication: is_url_safe() must reject a URL whose parsed authority carries credentials and must judge the same scheme/host the caller will dial, not a string it rewrote (src/helpers.ts:504-542).

Redirect adjudication: is_redirect_safe() must apply the same protocol and internal-host checks to the URL it was given and to every Location hop, and must check the URL it actually requests (src/helpers.ts:451-486).

Internal-address classification: is_hostname_resolve_to_internal_ip()/is_ip_internal() must resolve the host being dialled and flag loopback/private/link-local/metadata ranges, including rebinding (src/helpers.ts:225-265, src/helpers.ts:310-372).

Normalization must not move the authority: unicode/backslash/slash/@ rewrites run before parsing, so the parsed host must stay the host the raw input parses to (src/helpers.ts:378-418, src/helpers.ts:497-500).

Every shipped surface must carry the same adjudication: src/helpers.ts, the committed dist/helpers.js that package main loads, and the public re-exports in src/utils.ts (package.json:23, dist/utils.js:4, src/utils.ts:19-20).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: dist/ is tsc output, so hand-editing it looks wrong; the fix is to change src/helpers.ts and run npm run build (which the pinned tsconfig may not even do cleanly)

Redirect checking is an opt-in extra that is off unless DSSRF_CHECK_REDIRECTS=1 and README.md:82 advises against enabling it, so it reads as the non-security path; it also only ever requests the string it evaluated
Its own FIXME at src/helpers.ts:545 says the debug version does not match is_url_safe and is deliberately kept as is; the advisory only names is_url_safe

Removing '@' from the whole URL is the project's advertised userinfo defence (README.md:39) and remove_at_symbol_in_string is a public export used by the bench suite, so the stripper looks like intended behaviour that must not be removed

A name that does not resolve cannot be dialled, so returning not-internal on an empty answer is treated as harmless - and it is what lets any hostname, including legitimate ones, pass in an offline harness
Redirect checks are documented as off by default and privacy-sensitive (README.md:82), so the dead DSSRF_MAKE_REQUEST variable reads as a documentation bug rather than a missing URL check

masking: T1's fix hides T6: once parsed userinfo is rejected, the unresolvable stripped host built at src/helpers.ts:515 is never consulted for userinfo payloads, so the DNS fail-open at src/helpers.ts:337 stops being observable through the advisory's route.

T4 masks itself: is_url_safe_debug returns false for the advisory payload because its unconditional is_redirect_safe call (src/helpers.ts:546) fails closed on the stripped host (src/helpers.ts:463), so the missing check inside the debug twin is invisible to a behavioural test.

T3 is masked by the gate at src/helpers.ts:533: is_url_safe only calls is_redirect_safe when DSSRF_CHECK_REDIRECTS=1, and the helper itself fails closed on the stripped initial URL, so its missing check rarely changes an answer.

T2 masks T1 in the shipped package: if the harness loads package main (package.json:23 -> dist/utils.js:4 -> dist/helpers.js:430), a correct src/helpers.ts fix has no observable effect on is_url_safe.

conflicts.what: A string-level fix (strip or reject any '@' at src/helpers.ts:510) closes T1 but refuses legitimate path/query '@' values such as https://example.com/@alice or ?email=a@b.com; only a rule on the parsed username/password keeps both.

Making the resolver fail closed on an empty answer (src/helpers.ts:337) also kills the '@' bypass, but then every hostname is rejected in an offline harness, including the legitimate URLs the rest of the suite needs accepted.

Adding the userinfo rejection to is_url_safe_debug still leaves its unconditional is_redirect_safe call (src/helpers.ts:546), so the debug API keeps making outbound HEAD requests; making is_redirect_safe honour DSSRF_MAKE_REQUEST changes documented behaviour.

The src fix only reaches the loaded artefact if a build is run and succeeds; the pinned tsconfig.json:1-12 lacks rootDir and declarationMap yet dist/helpers.d.ts.map:1 exists, so the committed dist was not produced by this config and a rebuild may differ or fail.

fairness_risks: Rejecting any URL that contains '@' would refuse legitimate paths and queries such as https://example.com/@alice and https://api.example.com/v1/users?email=a@b.com; the rule must key on parsed username/password, not the raw character (src/helpers.ts:510).

The correct rule (refuse any parsed userinfo) also refuses legitimate basic-auth URLs such as http://user:pass@internal-reporting.example/, a shape some callers rely on; dssrf offers no other way to carry credentials.

Offline, is_hostname_resolve_to_internal_ip returns false whenever the lookup yields nothing (src/helpers.ts:337), which is the only reason is_url_safe('https://example.com') is true in a sandbox; a solver who hardens that to fail closed breaks every legitimate non-IP URL, so the fail-open is load-bearing for the test suite.

remove_at_symbol_in_string is a public export (src/utils.ts:16) and is exercised by benches/ssrf-validation.bench.ts:137-141, so the fix must stop calling it rather than delete it; deletion breaks the published API and the bench file.

A behavioural test using http://user@127.0.0.1/ cannot distinguish the pinned code from a fixed one: the stripped string 'http://user127.0.0.1/' fails URL parsing at src/helpers.ts:515 and is caught at src/helpers.ts:539, so the pinned code already returns false. A fair test has to use a named internal host (e.g. http://user@localhost/), where the stripped host parses and the DNS fail-open returns not-internal.

is_url_safe_debug makes an outbound HEAD request through is_redirect_safe with no gate (src/helpers.ts:546 -> src/helpers.ts:463) although README.md:82 promises no request unless DSSRF_MAKE_REQUEST=1; any test calling it must tolerate network or mock got().

design.why: One judgement per dismissal reason, not five copies of one grep. T1 is the reported route: parse the raw URL and reject parsed credentials instead of stripping '@' (src/helpers.ts:506-510, 515). T5 is T1's coupled must-keep-working value: '@' in path/query must stay acceptable and the public remove_at_symbol_in_string export (src/utils.ts:16) must stay callable, which rules out the tempting over-broad fix. T2 is the same vulnerability in the artefact the package actually loads (package.json:23 -> dist/utils.js:4 -> dist/helpers.js:430), dismissed as 'generated, just rebuild'. T3 is the public redirect entry point (src/helpers.ts:451-456), dismissed as 'opt-in and off by default'. T4 is the exported debug twin (src/helpers.ts:545-546), dismissed by its own FIXME. That spans both model weaknesses: DeepSeek's absent-protection-plus-dismissal routes (T2, T4) and MiMo's over-hardening of a coupled value (T5, with T1 exposing it). All sites sit in one 550-line file plus its committed build, so a careful engineer needs about an hour and the instance tests judgement rather than searching. Weaker alternatives: editing only src/helpers.ts collapses T1/T3/T4 into one edit and never exercises the shipped dist, and adding T6 (src/helpers.ts:337) is unusable because fail-closed DNS contradicts every offline hostname test. Caveat: T2 only bites if the harness loads the package root; if it imports src/ directly, T2 degrades to a rebuild step and the design is T1/T3/T4/T5, with T3/T4 only observable if the harness mocks got() or asserts on the exported functions' code path.

unverified: The fix commit 9211f91 and any fix.diff are not present in the worktree and no advisory text is committed, so every statement about what the published fix did (shared parsed-URL helper, tsconfig patch, hand-edited dist) comes from the screener record, not from the pinned tree.

Whether npm run build (typescript 6.0.2) succeeds at the pinned commit: no shell in this session. tsconfig.json:1-12 sets declaration but not declarationMap, yet dist/helpers.d.ts.map:1 exists, so the committed dist was not produced by this exact configuration.
Whether the grading harness loads dist (package.json:23, the honest package surface) or imports src/: this decides whether T1 or T2 is the graded surface and whether a rebuild is required.

WHATWG parser claims were reasoned about, not executed: new URL('http://user127.0.0.1/') is expected to throw (numeric last label forces IPv4 parsing, non-numeric earlier labels fail), while new URL('http://userlocalhost/') parses as a domain; the pinned node was not run.

Offline DNS behaviour and timing were not measured; resolveWithDelay sleeps 100-300 ms and is called twice (src/helpers.ts:320-333), and node_modules is absent from the tree, so one networked install of got/ip-cidr/ipaddr.js/typescript is needed before any run.
